title: Incoming shipment lag analysis & scheduling — GPU procurement pipeline workbook
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet analyzes recent inbound GPU shipment lags, quantifies lead-time variance by SKU and region, and proposes a short-term scheduling plan to minimize burst outages while keeping committed spend within budget windows. NOT final — iterative analysis; use as input to next supply sync (Thu ops sync).

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Three high-risk lanes: APAC SEA (customs delays), EU-West freight consolidation, US-West port congestion.
- Median lead-time drift since Q3 2025: +12 days (weighted by order value). 90th percentile drift: +28 days.
- Near-term actions: prioritize 40% of urgent replenish orders onto air-lift lanes for critical SKUs (A100-80GB, H100-80GB), move noncritical S35 series to deferred sea shipments.

Assumptions used in the sheet:
- Baseline lead time = vendor promise + typical transit + customs buffer (30 days baseline for sea to EU/NA; 7 days baseline for air).
- Burn rate per region taken from 'regional-gpu-burnrate-2025Q4' (internal sheet).
- Buffer policy target: 14-day availability buffer for hosted API lanes; 21-day for Dedicated pools.
- Currency/price holds not considered here (separate finance delta sheet).

Table: inbound orders (working view)
Columns: OrderID | SKU | Vendor | Region | Qty (units) | Qty (GPU-days est) | Orig ETA | Latest ETA | Lead time delta (days) | Transit mode | Status | Priority | Risk flag
1. ORD-2025-117 | A100-80GB | Vendor-X | US-WEST | 40 | 12,000 | 2025-12-18 | 2026-01-08 | +21 | sea -> port | in_transit | high | port-backlog
2. ORD-2025-129 | H100-80GB | Vendor-Y | EU-WEST | 16 | 9,600 | 2026-01-04 | 2026-01-15 | +11 | air | shipped | urgent | consolidation-delay
3. ORD-2026-003 | S35 | Vendor-Z | APAC-SEA | 80 | 6,400 | 2026-01-22 | 2026-02-10 | +19 | sea | pending | medium | customs-risk
4. ORD-2025-088 | A100-80GB (refurb) | Vendor-Q | US-EAST | 24 | 7,200 | 2025-12-05 | 2025-12-30 | +25 | sea | received (partial) | medium | inspection-hold
5. ORD-2026-012 | H100-80GB | Vendor-Y | EU-NORDIC | 8 | 4,800 | 2026-01-10 | 2026-01-11 | +1 | air | shipped | low | none
6. ORD-2026-021 | A100-80GB | Vendor-P | APAC-JPN | 12 | 3,600 | 2026-01-20 | 2026-02-08 | +19 | sea | pending | high | port-surge

Calculated fields notes (manual check):
- Lead time delta: latest ETA - orig ETA (days). Positive = delay.
- Qty (GPU-days est) = Qty * avg_gpu_days_per_unit (A100/H100 -> 300, S-series -> 80).
- Risk flag uses combined heuristic: (delay > 15 OR region in known hotspot) AND (SKU in critical_list) -> escalate.

Observed patterns and root-cause hypotheses (working):
- Consolidation holidays in EU vendors caused multi-week batching delays; several air-lanes used by the same forwarder saturated in Jan 2026.
- Port backups in US-WEST increased dwell time by 7–14 days; many vendors re-routing shipments to alternate ports without notifying procurement lead (process gap).
- APAC customs queue variability correlates with documentation mismatches from refurbished lots — inspection rate increased.

Short-term schedule proposal (2–6 weeks):
1) Immediate rebook: Move ORD-2025-117 (40 A100) from sea to mixed air-consolidated lanes for 40% of volume -> expected recovery of 14 days. Cost delta estimate attached in finance sheet.
2) Hold-and-batch: Delay S35 noncritical orders (ORD-2026-003) to next 3-week sea window to free carrier slots for H100/A100 urgent moves.
3) Staging reallocation: Reassign Dedicated pool margin in EU-West to accept partial receipts from ORD-2025-129 to reduce failover to fallback model variants.
4) Customs remediation: Vendor-Z to supply standardized inspection packet for refurbished SKUs within 48 hours; escalate to vendor SLO.

Medium-term tweaks (1–3 months):
- Rebalance SKU mix in APAC to prefer locally sourceable mid-tier GPUs (reduce long-haul sea dependency).
- Introduce vendor performance SLAs with explicit notification windows (T+3 alert for ETA drift > 7 days).
- Experiment with staggered monthly ordering windows to avoid peak consolidation days (proposal in column schedule_proposals).

Risk matrix (quick):
- High financial risk: Rebooking to air for 40% of ORD-2025-117 -> increases unit cost ~3.2x; but avoids Dedicated pool outages estimated cost > $200k in SLO penalties.
- Operational risk: Inspection/QA for refurbished units causing 3–7 day internal hold; mitigate by parallel QA lanes at receiving site.
- Compliance risk: APAC customs documentation for refurb units; short-term fix as above; long-term vendor onboarding checklist needed.

Open questions / TODOs (owner in parens):
- Confirm finance approval for air-rebook for ORD-2025-117 (Elliot) — deadline: 2026-02-22.
- Can Vendor-X provide partial early shipments from alternate warehouses? (Priya)
- Verify burn-rate shift if 40% of A100 capacity delayed 21+ days — run sim and post numbers to JIRA-INFRA-1897 (Mateo).
- Add TTL column for per-order escalation (owner: procurement lead).

Appendix: quick calculation snippets (manual):
- If ORD-2025-117 40 units air 40% -> 16 units air -> 16*300 gpu-days = 4,800 gpu-days expedited; expected recoverable buffer = 14 days * average throughput (calc in finance sheet).
- 90th percentile lead time by recent window: sea_to_eu = 46 days; sea_to_na = 52 days; air lanes = 12 days (with variability +/- 4d).

Meeting notes snapshot (ops sync 2026-02-20):
- Procurement will push vendor-notification template to all vendors by EOD Mon; ops to build emergency air budget window for Feb-Mar.
- SRE requested visibility into partial receipts stream to avoid automated capacity drains; implementation ticket created (JIRA-INFRA-1904).

Version history (working):
- v0.1 2025-11-05 initial import of inbound ledger
- v0.7 2026-01-12 added regional risk flags after customs surge in APAC
- v0.9 2026-02-02 applied port backlog reschedule recommendations
- v1.0 2026-02-20 current working version (this doc)

Notes to self: this sheet is intentionally conservative on buffers for Dedicated pools. If finance pushes back on air spend, we will need to produce a prioritized rollback list of application-level fallbacks (list to create).

End of workbook (working) — comments inline.
